new_roles.title: Director, Commercial Operations and Asset Management
new_roles.description:
**SUMMARY:** The Director, Commercial Operations & Asset Management provides leadership over the operational execution and ongoing asset management of Rhyze’s Commercial lending platform. This role is accountable for establishing scalable, controlled processes across transaction closing, funding, participation, servicing and portfolio administration, while actively overseeing the performance, credit quality and risk profile of the commercial real estate loan portfolio.

The Director leads portfolio surveillance, borrower and property performance monitoring, covenant compliance, annual review coordination, delinquency management and the operational execution of workout and loss mitigation strategies. The position works closely with the Managing Director, Commercial; Capital Markets; and Legal, and coordinates with lead lenders, borrowers, servicing partners and participating credit unions as appropriate.

The successful candidate combines commercial real estate credit and asset management expertise with operational discipline, sound judgment, strong communication skills and a focus on scalable execution.

**DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Commercial Portfolio & Asset Management**

· Lead portfolio surveillance and risk-based monitoring of commercial real estate loans, including payment performance, DSCR, net operating income, occupancy, rent rolls, leasing, borrower liquidity, maturities and concentration exposure.

· Oversee borrower and property financial reporting, covenant testing and compliance calendars; identify reporting deficiencies, covenant breaches, emerging risks and required follow-up.

· Coordinate annual and interim credit reviews, risk-rating assessments, watchlist management and action plans, with documented findings, ownership, deadlines and management escalation.

· Oversee collateral protection requirements, including insurance, property taxes, escrows, reserves, liens, property inspections, appraisals and other third-party assessments, in coordination with Servicing and Legal.

**Special Assets & Loss Mitigation**

· Identify and escalate delinquencies, maturity or covenant defaults and deteriorating credits; coordinate borrower outreach, collection strategies and remediation plans for criticized or classified assets.

· Evaluate requests for waivers, modifications, extensions, forbearances and other accommodations; develop supporting analysis and recommendations for authorized decision-makers.

· Coordinate workout and loss mitigation activities with Commercial leadership, Legal and external counsel, including enforcement, bankruptcy or foreclosure matters when applicable.

· Prepare required participant notices and approval packages; document borrower communications, decisions, conditions and deadlines, and monitor execution and performance under approved resolution plans.

**Commercial Operations & Servicing Oversight**

· Lead day-to-day Commercial operations with clear accountability, service standards, quality controls and escalation procedures across the loan lifecycle.

· Oversee transaction closing, funding, loan boarding and post-closing administration, including conditions, documentation, milestone tracking, data transfers and outstanding exceptions.

· Coordinate with internal teams, servicing partners and Capital Markets on participation administration, payment processing, reconciliations, escrows, reserves, borrower notices, payoffs, releases and related servicing matters.

· Ensure accurate implementation and recording of approved modifications, extensions and other post-closing actions, consistent with loan documents, participation agreements, delegated authority and applicable requirements.

**Operational Excellence, Reporting & Scalability**

· Provide timely loan-level and portfolio reporting to management and participating investors, including delinquencies, covenant exceptions, watchlist activity, material credit events and remediation progress.

· Serve as a central coordinator across Commercial, Capital Markets, Finance, Legal, servicing partners, lead lenders and participating credit unions on operational and portfolio matters.

· Develop and standardize procedures, controls, checklists, templates and reporting; identify opportunities for automation, integration and improved data quality to support scalable growth.

· Establish and monitor key performance indicators, including reporting compliance, review completion, exception aging, delinquency trends, watchlist resolution and transaction cycle times.

**Other**· Responsible for effective self/workload management. Demonstrates clear written and verbal communication skills. Promotes collaboration and a positive, professional work environment. Attends all position related meetings to ensure proper communication/planning occurs.

· Performs other related duties as assigned by the Managing Director

· Complies with all company policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.

· Care for non-public information (NPI) and ensuring that confidentiality of company, borrowers, and partner information is maintained.

· Responsible for contributing to a positive work environment and culture that represents the company values.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

· Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field preferred; equivalent professional experience considered.

· Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in commercial real estate lending, commercial credit administration, loan servicing, asset management, or a related field, with demonstrated experience managing commercial loan portfolios.

· Strong understanding of the end-to-end commercial lending lifecycle, including loan documentation, closing, funding, servicing, portfolio administration, and loan participations.

· Demonstrated expertise in commercial real estate asset management, including financial statement analysis, property performance monitoring, debt service coverage, covenant compliance, collateral valuation, and credit risk assessment.

· Experience identifying and managing problem loans, including delinquencies, covenant defaults, borrower accommodations, forbearances, modifications, workouts, and loss mitigation strategies.

· Strong knowledge of commercial loan servicing practices, including payment administration, escrow and reserve management, collateral protection, and post-closing compliance.

· Demonstrated ability to evaluate portfolio performance, identify emerging credit risks, develop actionable recommendations, and effectively communicate findings to management and other stakeholders.

· Experience establishing and improving operational processes, internal controls, reporting practices, and technology-enabled workflows to support efficiency, accuracy, and scalability.

· Strong understanding of commercial lending regulatory requirements, credit policies, risk management practices, and financial institution governance.

· Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, coordinate cross-functional activities, and lead complex initiatives with a high degree of accountability and attention to detail.

· Excellent analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and communication skills, with the ability to effectively engage borrowers, lending partners, credit union executives, and internal stakeholders.

· Self-motivated, adaptable, and comfortable operating independently in an entrepreneurial, growth-oriented environment.

Pay: $165,000.00 - $185,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

Work Location: Remote

**POSITION Description**

**Manager/Director of Quality**

**Title:** Manager/Director of Quality

**Location:** Rochester, NY

**Company:** EvolvOptic is a leading supplier of precision machined optical blanks. We are shaping the future together with our collaborators and customers. We are growing our capacity and capabilities for blank manufacturing. The same experienced team that made our company a respected leader in our field remains on the frontlines, keeping production humming and delivering an array of high-quality components. We are proud and honored to be a partner to our customers for their optical component needs providing best-value solutions to meet their priorities, including cost, schedule, and assured quality.

The forecast for the future is bright. We are expanding into large, complex optical components by pulling together the right team, the right technology, and the right methods to provide best-value solutions to ground-based and space-based imaging, semiconductor industry, and high energy optics, such as laser fusion and directed energy.

**Position Summary**

The Manager/ Director of Quality is a senior leadership position responsible for developing and executing EvolvOptic's quality strategy and ensuring the highest standards of product quality, measurement integrity, and operational excellence across the organization. Reporting directly to the President, this role provides strategic and technical leadership for quality assurance and compliance.

**Leadership Expectations**

Serve as a member of the executive leadership team, driving a culture of quality, accountability, continuous improvement, and customer satisfaction while enabling EvolvOptic's growth in commercial space, aerospace, defense, semiconductor, and scientific optics markets.

**Primary Responsibilities**

* Develop and execute the company's quality strategy aligned with business objectives.
* Provide executive leadership for Quality, Inspection, Calibration and Compliance functions.
* Lead and continuously improve the QMS and all audit activities.
* Establish quality KPIs and drive CAPA, root cause analysis, and operational excellence.
* Lead supplier quality and serve as the senior customer quality interface.
* Support proposals, NPI, program execution, and manufacturing readiness reviews.
* Build and mentor a high-performing Quality organization.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in a relevant engineering or scientific discipline; advanced degree preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive quality, metrology, or manufacturing leadership experience.
* 5+ years in a management or director-level leadership role.
* Experience in precision optics, aerospace, defense, semiconductor, or scientific instrumentation preferred.
* Strong knowledge of optical manufacturing, advanced metrology, ISO 9001, AS9100, SPC, MSA, FMEA, and GD&T.

**Key Competencies**

* Technical credibility with engineers and manufacturing teams
* Strong organizational and prioritization skills
* Clear, concise written and verbal communication
* Risk-driven decision making
* Adaptability and comfort with ambiguity

This position is subject to US export control laws, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and the Export Administration Regulations (EAR), which require US person status. A “US person” is defined by these regulations as a US citizen, US lawful permanent resident (i.e., “green card holder”), political asylee, or refugee.

All employees must also be legally authorized to work in the United States. Verification of employment eligibility will be required consistent with federal law (Form I-9). Export control assessments are conducted separately to ensure compliance with ITAR/EAR.

EvolvOptic is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected status or characteristic protected by state or federal law.

Pay: $100,000.00 - $135,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

new_roles.title: Senior Director, Operations
new_roles.description:
We’re looking for people who put their innovation to work to advance our success – and their own. Join an organization that ensures a more secure world through connecting and protecting our customers with inventive electrical solutions.

The Senior Director, Operations is a strategic operations leadership role responsible for scaling a $1.5B+ manufacturing campus and multi-site footprint through digital transformation, operational excellence, and high-impact leadership to enable accelerated growth and customer value. While this role carries responsibility for long-term operational strategy, digital transformation, capacity planning, and Smart Factory initiatives, the immediate mandate is centered on stabilizing and transforming one of nVent's most important manufacturing operations globally. The Anoka campus represents approximately $1.5 billion in annual revenue and employs roughly 1,700 people today, with expected growth toward 2,000 employees in the coming years. It is the largest manufacturing operation in the United States and the second-largest globally within nVent's manufacturing network.

 

Reporting directly to the Vice President, Integrated Supply Chain of the Systems Protection Segment, this role will have significant visibility across the organization and will play a critical role in shaping the future operating model of one of nVent's most strategically important manufacturing assets. Success in this role will create meaningful opportunities for broader enterprise leadership responsibility within nVent's global Integrated Supply Chain organization.

 

Key Responsibilities:

* Champion a high-performance continuous improvement culture by embedding Lean and problem-solving disciplines across all levels of the organization; empower employees to identify waste, implement solutions, and deliver sustainable gains while formally recognizing exceptional performance and contributions.
* Lead large-scale, multi-site operational transformation across a large scaled flagship campus and additional high-growth plants, ensuring alignment of capacity, capability, and talent strategies to support accelerated business growth and evolving customer demand.
* Drive Smart Factory / Digital Manufacturing advancement by scaling production capability through strategic investments in automation, advanced tooling, equipment, and data-driven systems (Industry 4.0), while balancing legacy operations with next-generation technologies to optimize throughput, quality, and cost.
* Own end-to-end operational performance across Operations, Procurement, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, Environmental Health & Safety (EHS), Facilities, Material Handling, and Business Support functions, ensuring disciplined execution against safety, quality, delivery, cost, and cash flow objectives
* Develop and execute integrated strategic business plans that translate enterprise objectives into site-level actions, including long-range capacity planning, capital deployment (CapEx), workforce strategy, and footprint optimization across multiple locations.
* Serve as a key leader and cross-functional partner, collaborating with senior leadership, supply chain, engineering, and commercial teams to align short- and long-term operational strategies, remove constraints, and ensure successful new product introductions and business expansion.
* Lead, coach, and inspire a large, diverse organization by building strong leadership benches, strengthening succession pipelines, and fostering accountability, engagement, and inclusion across all functions and sites.
* Leverage data and operational analytics to drive decision-making, identifying bottlenecks, improving asset utilization (OEE), optimizing material flow, and prioritizing high-impact investments that enable scalability and profitability.
* Establish robust communication channels and employee engagement mechanisms to proactively monitor organizational health, gather feedback, and address concerns in partnership with Human Resources—ensuring a strong, transparent, and trust-based culture across all locations.
* Ensure world-class safety, compliance, and sustainability performance, reinforcing a zero-harm culture while maintaining adherence to environmental regulations, responsible sourcing practices, and corporate governance standards.
* Establish and sustain a rigorous management operating system across the campus, including daily management, tiered accountability processes, visual management, structured problem solving, and disciplined escalation practices that enable rapid identification and resolution of operational issues.
* Drive stabilization and performance improvement initiatives across critical manufacturing lines, ensuring achievement of safety, quality, delivery, and productivity commitments while restoring operational predictability and customer confidence.
* Lead the continued development of a high-performance culture rooted in accountability, transparency, problem solving, and employee engagement, creating an environment where issues are surfaced early, addressed rapidly, and solved at their root cause.
* Evaluate and optimize material flow, production layout, workforce deployment, and capacity utilization across the campus, balancing immediate operational needs with long-term scalability requirements.
Partner closely with Quality, Engineering, Supply Chain, Lean, Human Resources, and Finance leaders to strengthen organizational capability, improve execution, and ensure alignment around operational priorities and business objectives. 

 

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES:

* The ideal candidate will bring a BA or BS degree in Business, Engineering or similar field; MBA or other graduate degree is preferred.
* Deep understanding of lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, and continuous improvement methodologies (TPM, Kaizen) within high-volume environments.
* Strong command of Smart Factory technologies, including IoT integration, predictive maintenance, automated material handling, and data-driven shop floor management.
* Comprehensive knowledge of EHS (Environmental, Health, and Safety) compliance, supply chain logistics, strategic procurement, and capital expenditure (CapEx) management.
* Expertise in long-range capacity planning, workforce strategy, and balancing the operational requirements of legacy product lines with the agility needed for new product introductions (NPI).
* Proficiency in P&L management, budget forecasting, and aligning plant-level performance metrics with enterprise-wide financial objectives.
* Ability to translate corporate strategy into actionable site-level plans and orchestrate cross-functional teams toward common goals.
* Demonstrated success in leading large-scale cultural and technical shifts, including the transition to digital manufacturing environments while maintaining stable output.
* Skill in leveraging operational analytics to identify bottlenecks, optimize production capability, and justify capital investments.
* Exceptional ability to foster open, transparent communication across all levels—from the shop floor to the executive boardroom—and effectively partner with Human Resources on organizational health.
* Proven ability to build, mentor, and inspire high-performing teams, fostering an environment of psychological safety and professional growth.
* Ability to navigate complex matrix organizations and collaborate effectively with stakeholders in Sales, Engineering, Finance, and HR to execute short- and long-term plans.
* Capacity to remain decisive and calm under pressure, managing the competing demands of high-growth production spikes, technical troubleshooting, and daily operational hurdles.•Ability to balance immediate, reactive operational needs with long-term, proactive improvements in infrastructure, tooling, and site facilities.
* Aptitude for cultivating a high-engagement, inclusive workplace that promotes active employee participation in problem-solving and recognizes performance excellence.

**WE HAVE:**

* A dynamic global reach with diverse operations around the world that will stretch your abilities, provide plentiful career opportunities, and allow you to make an impact every day

 + nVent is a leading global provider of electrical connection and protection solutions. We believe our inventive electrical solutions enable safer systems and ensure a more secure world. We design, manufacture, market, install and service high performance products and solutions that connect and protect some of the world's most sensitive equipment, buildings and critical processes. We offer a comprehensive range of systems protection and electrical connections solutions across industry-leading brands that are recognized globally for quality, reliability and innovation.
 + Our principal office is in London and our management office in the United States is in Minneapolis. Our robust portfolio of leading electrical product brands dates back more than 100 years and includes nVent CADDY, ERICO, HOFFMAN, ILSCO, SCHROFF and TRACHTE. Learn more at www.nvent.com .

* Commitment to strengthen communities where our employees live and work

 + We encourage and support the philanthropic activities of our employees worldwide
 + Through our nVent in Action matching program, we provide funds to nonprofit and educational organizations where our employees volunteer or donate money

* Core values that shape our culture and drive us to deliver the best for our employees and our customers. We’re known for being:

 + Innovative & adaptable
 + Dedicated to absolute integrity
 + Focused on the customer first
 + Respectful and team oriented
 + Optimistic and energizing
 + Accountable for performance

* Benefits to support the lives of our employees

**Pay Transparency** 
 
nVent’s pay scale is based on the expected range of base pay for this job and the employee’s work location. Employee pay within this range will be based on a combination of factors including knowledge, skills, abilities, experience, education, and performance. Where federal, state, or local minimum wage requirements exist, employee pay will comply.
 
 
**Compensation Range:**

$204,400.00 - $304,000.00

Depending on the position offered, employee may be eligible for other forms of compensation, such as annual incentives.

**Benefit Overview**

new_roles.title: NPI Director North America - Solutions
new_roles.description:
*Join the worldwide leader in playing cards and in “play” solutions. Play is what keeps us going, and it always has been our greatest motivation. That's why we* ***live different****,* ***play different****.*

We are seeking an experienced **NPI Director North America - Solutions** to provide regional leadership for New Product Introduction across North America, covering the relevant manufacturing sites and Design Center capabilities. The role translates business and customer priorities into a coherent NPI strategy, governance model and project portfolio, ensuring that new products move from concept to stable commercialization with the required quality, cost, timing, compliance and manufacturability. The role aligns Commercial, Global Design Center, NPI, Engineering, R&D, Quality, Procurement and Manufacturing and develops the capabilities required for consistent execution across sites..

**Key Responsibilities:**

**NPI strategy and governance**

* Translate the global NPI strategy into the North American operating model, stage-gate governance, priorities and decision routines, aligned with the Global Accounts and Global Design Center Director.
* Own the North American NPI portfolio and facilitate prioritization, resource allocation, escalation and trade-off decisions across customer programs and manufacturing sites in the region.
* Implement and continuously improve common global standards, templates, performance measures and management routines for product development, prototyping, design transfer, validation and industrialization.
* Ensure early NPI and Design Center involvement in strategic customer opportunities and new product concepts.

**Portfolio delivery and industrialization**

* Oversee major and complex NPI programs from concept through commercialization and stable production handover.
* Ensure projects have clear business cases, requirements, milestones, risks, accountabilities and readiness criteria.
* Drive design-for-manufacturing, cost engineering, value engineering and manufacturability reviews before production commitment.
* Ensure product concepts are technically feasible, compliant, financially viable and transferable across the relevant North American manufacturing network, while ensuring effective transfer to or from other regions when required.
* Lead executive-level reviews of portfolio status, critical risks, capacity constraints and recovery plans.

**Cross-functional and customer leadership**

* Act as the senior NPI interface for strategic customer programs and align customer expectations with operational capabilities.
* Build strong collaboration across Commercial, Business Development, Design, Engineering, R&D, Quality, Procurement, Supply Chain and Manufacturing.
* Coordinate North American and global resources to resolve cross-functional issues and accelerate decision making.
* Promote disciplined change control and transparent communication throughout the development and industrialization process.

**Capability and team leadership**

* Lead, coach and develop the North American NPI organization with teams in Seattle, Dallas and East-Longmeadow, including regional managers, project leaders and specialist resources.
* Build project management, product industrialization, risk management and technical problem-solving capabilities.
* Contribute to global communities of practice and promote best-practice sharing across North American sites and with other regions.
* Foster a culture of customer focus, innovation, accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.

**Qualifications and Requirements:**

* Master’s degree in engineering, manufacturing, product development, business or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* Significant leadership experience in NPI, product development, engineering, industrialization or complex program management within a multi-site manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated experience establishing governance, managing portfolios and leading major cross-functional product introductions.
* Strong commercial awareness and ability to balance customer value, technical feasibility, operational risk and financial performance.
* Excellent communication, influencing and decision-making skills in an international and multicultural environment.
* Fluent professional English; additional languages are an advantage. Ability to travel across North America and internationally when required.

Benefits an **NPI Director North America – Solutions** can expect from Cartamundi:

* Competitive pay
* Climate controlled facility
* 401(k) with company match
* Health, dental, and vision insurance starting day one
* HSA (Health Savings Account) and FSA (Flexible Savings Account)
* Life insurance
* Short-Term and Long-Term Disability
* Paid time off
* Tuition reimbursement
* Employee discounts on daycare, gym memberships, travel, and much more

**Apply today and discover the magic of making a difference at Cartamundi!**

*Cartamundi does not discriminate based on race, sex, color, religion, age, national origin, marital status, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity or any other reason prohibited by law in provision of employment opportunities.* *This employer participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. For more information on E-Verify, or if you believe that your employer has violated its E-Verify responsibilities, please contact DHS* *dhs.gov/e-verify**.*

*Candidates must be 18 years old to work for Cartamundi.*

*No agencies please. No sponsorship available.*

**About Cartamundi:**

At Cartamundi, we're all united by our common belief that world is better with play. Play is what keeps us going, and it always has been our greatest motivation. That's why we live different and play different. To us, it is not just an activity. It is a guiding mindset that reminds us to have fun, to be fair, to connect with people – across cultures and generations – and to embrace shared experiences.

We are a worldwide leader in playing cards and in “play” solutions.

Our owned brand portfolio includes a suite of heritage brands which go back as far as 1848, including global brands like Bicycle®, HRO®, Bee®, Copag®, Shuffle® and many locally loved brands. These brands combine craftsmanship with innovation as the basis for their continued relevance and positive contribution to the local communities that love and use these brands.

At Cartamundi, we have significant expertise in printing; our presses have been running since 1765. Today, our company has become the largest playing cards and board game manufacturer in the world and the trusted partner of leading toy companies. We make well-known brands such as Monopoly®, Uno®, Magic: The Gathering®, Guess Who ®, Pokémon®, Trivial Pursuit® every day.

As we look into the future and how entertainment evolves, we are bringing the digital world to the physical world and vice versa. We have a dedicated team of experts that is looking into future technologies, products, and applications that can get our consumers and communities to truly live different and play different.

We are still a family-owned company with headquarters in Belgium and have a global network of 16 manufacturing facilities, 6 design centers, 1 digital studio and 1 global R&D center

new_roles.title: Sr. Director Operations Engineering - C&I
new_roles.description:
**We believe power is a promise - a shared commitment to be there for others when it matters most.**
====================================================================================================

For more than 65 years, we've turned big ideas into solutions that help protect homes, strengthen businesses and build a more resilient, efficient, sustainable energy future.

Ready to Power a Smarter World with us?

**Sr Director, Operations Engineering**
=======================================

The Sr Director, Operations Engineering is responsible for leading the enterprise Operations Engineering function with a focus on New Product Launches, Operations Integrations, Product Moves, and Operations Standards. This role ensures that new products, newly integrated operations, and transferred products are launched and sustained in manufacturing safely, on time, at quality, and at target cost. Through the development and deployment of enterprise standards, best practices, and the Generac Fulfillment System (GFS), the Director drives consistent, world-class execution across the Order-to-Cash process (Plan, Source, Make, Deliver & Service). The role partners closely with Engineering, Advanced Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, Finance, HR, and Business Unit leadership, and supports Generac's global manufacturing portfolio.

**Major Responsibilities**
--------------------------

### **New Product Launches (NPI)**

* Lead and coordinate the successful launch of New Product Introductions (NPI) within operations, from early design involvement through production ramp and sustained performance.
* Ensure manufacturing readiness for new products, including process design, PFMEA, line layout, tooling, fixtures, work instructions, and capacity planning.
* Partner with Product Engineering to drive design for manufacturability and assembly so new products launch with optimal cost, quality, and delivery.
* Establish launch gates, readiness criteria, and success metrics, and hold cross-functional teams accountable to them.
* Lead and support the introduction of new and revised processes and technologies that support cost reduction and competitive advantage.

### **Operations Integrations**

* Lead the operational integration of new sites, acquisitions, and expanded capacity into the Generac manufacturing network, aligning processes, systems, and performance expectations.
* Lead and contribute to facility transformation, including layout, mixed-model lines, value stream design, and deployment of the Generac Fulfillment System (GFS).
* Assess integrated facilities, infrastructure systems, and technology against best-in-class capability and develop roadmaps to close gaps.
* Coordinate cross-functional collaboration with HR, Finance, Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, and senior leadership to ensure integrations meet business objectives.
* Incorporate workplace optimization, space planning, and long-term facility planning into integration plans.

### **Product Moves & Transfers**

* Lead the planning and execution of product moves and technology transfers between facilities and with external supply chain partners, ensuring continuity of supply, quality, and cost.
* Own and continuously improve the product transfer procedure, and support the Operations Product Transfer Steering Committee to ensure alignment and adherence to the procedure.
* Develop transfer plans that include capacity validation, equipment and tooling relocation, process validation, training, and inventory bridge strategies.
* Partner with Business Unit and Manufacturing Strategy leaders to support footprint, rebalancing, and new capacity decisions with sound operations engineering analysis.

### **Operations Standards**

* Develop with corporate Advanced Manufacturing, deploy, and sustain enterprise operations engineering standards, policies, procedures, and process documentation that drive consistent execution across all facilities.
* Drive significant contributions to the implementation of the Generac Fulfillment System (GFS) across the Order-to-Cash process.
* Develop and implement operating methodologies designed to maximize floor space utilization, asset uptime and utilization, eliminate waste, and reduce operating cost.
* Champion lean principles and continuous improvement, and ensure the ongoing success of process improvement initiatives.
* Establish and monitor KPIs to evaluate productivity, engineering output, launch performance, and facility efficiency, using data to drive improvement.
* Ensure compliance with safety, quality, and environmental standards, and incorporate sustainability and energy efficiency initiatives.

### **Project Management & Financial Stewardship**

* Drive and project manage major cost, quality, and delivery initiatives, with a strong focus on breakthrough process and technology improvements.
* Facilitate project flow through regular engagement with engineering, manufacturing, and other cross-functional teams, managing shifting priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
* Oversee capital projects related to launches, integrations, and product moves, and provide budgetary figures for future fiscal year planning.
* Manage the operations engineering budget and support reduction of the operating cost of each facility consistent with company objectives.

### **Leadership & Talent Development**

* Lead the Operations Engineering team, including project planning, technical guidance, and resource allocation across sites and initiatives.
* Select, coach, and develop a high-performing team of engineers and project managers, setting objectives that align with company strategy.
* Manage organizational talent through performance management, succession planning, and development, ensuring feedback is consistently delivered and performance is systematically improved.
* Provide guidance to cross-functional teams and leadership on key decisions related to investment in core manufacturing technologies, processes, and systems.

**Minimum Job Requirements**
----------------------------

* **Education:** Bachelor's Degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Electrical, or Industrial) or Industrial Technology.
* **Work Experience:** 10+ years of related experience in Operations Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, and Production, including leading new product launches and product transfers.
* **Leadership Experience:** 5+ years of increasing responsibility for project and/or people management involving a broad range of operational technologies and processes.

**Knowledge / Skills / Abilities**
----------------------------------

* Strong knowledge of New Product Development, PFMEA, and operations engineering principles.
* Knowledge of lean principles, continuous improvement, and end-to-end supply chain principles.
* Experience operating in both high-mix, low-volume and high-volume, low-mix production environments.
* Ability to assess and manage end-to-end processes and to manage strategic and tactical issues by being hands-on.
* Ability to develop and deploy standards and best practices across multiple sites.
* Ability to attract, develop, and manage an impactful team.
* Demonstrated skills in problem solving, conflict resolution, and cross-functional collaboration.
* Excellent organizational, written, and oral communication skills, including the ability to influence senior leadership.
* Proven ability to prioritize multiple projects with shifting priorities and moving deadlines.
* Proficiency in a CAD platform (AutoCAD, SolidWorks, and/or ProE), MS Office, and ERP platforms.

**Preferred Job Requirements**
------------------------------

* Master's Degree in Mechanical, Electrical, or Industrial Engineering.
* Project Management certification (e.g., PMP).
* Experience deploying processes and standards at an enterprise level, both internally and with external supply chain partners.
* Experience leading operations integrations, facility transformations, and multi-site product transfers.
* Experience working in an international company and in matrix organizations, with multi-site support experience.
* Previous experience using SAP or an equivalent ERP.
* Experience with facilities engineering and with using and/or implementing CMMS systems.
* Large-scale project management experience.

*“We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.”*

new_roles.description:
**Everything we do is underscored by a why — and that why is one another.**

**Location:**

Altru Hospital,1200 South Columbia Road,Grand Forks, ND 58201

**Summary:**

The Director of Quality and Safety provides strategic leadership for organizational quality, patient safety, regulatory compliance, and performance improvement initiatives. This role partners with physicians, clinical leaders, and operational stakeholders to develop and implement programs that advance patient outcomes, ensure regulatory readiness, mitigate risk, and foster a culture of safety and continuous improvement. The Director oversees quality and safety operations, drives achievement of organizational and financial goals, ensures compliance with applicable regulatory standards, and leads the development of high-performing teams dedicated to delivering exceptional care and operational excellence. Through collaboration, innovation, and data-driven decision making, this position supports Altru's commitment to quality, safety, and outstanding patient experiences.
 
 
A master's degree and experience managing cross-functional teams including guiding clinical and administrative employees preferred

**Essential Job Functions:**

* Develops and implements long-range goals that enhance services and support strong relational management with key stakeholders. Develops collaborative relationships with leadership, physicians, clinical, professional and support staff. Sets standards for operational performance for the division/department(s) and fiscal accountability. Develops and achieves annual financial targets and holds managers and employees accountable to budget targets.
* Oversees the facilitation of regulatory requirements identified internally or from external agencies. Oversees the reporting and submission of regulatory compliance to external agencies as required through contractual relationships.
* Maintains competency in all organizational, department standards relevant to services provided.
* Practices process improvement principles and while managing processes to ensure all regulatory standards are met, and accesses internal resources to assist in adhering to standards as well as ensuring staff understand expectations
* Recruits, develops, retains and leads a talented team of leadership and staff committed to accomplishing the goals of Altru Health System. Builds an environment of shared commitment to organizational goals and fosters an environment conducive to maximizing individual and collective productivity, emphasizing performance and collaboration. Conducts performance reviews, actively recognizes and rewards employees and takes appropriate actions when performance is not meeting expectations. Acts as a mentor and promotes professional growth of employees. Takes responsibility for personal growth and development and meets all system educational requirements.
* Seeks out operational efficiency and involves employees and physicians in workforce redesign, as appropriate to better serve the patient, as well as create a workplace that all employees can function at their highest competency and productivity. Leads and participates in acquisition of new technologies to ensure the highest standard of care.
* Maintains competency in all organizational, department and outside agency standards relevant to services provided and ensures compliance. Manages processes to ensure all regulatory standards are met as well as works to prevent potential legal risk to Altru Health System as appropriate. Accesses internal resources to assist in adhering to standards as well as ensures staff understands expectations.
* Performs other duties as assigned or needed to meet the needs of the department/organization.

### **Certifications**

**Job Description**

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

**LOCATION**: Currently tied to Morrisville, NC (may be open to other locations). Relocation assistance is NOT provided.

* Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.
* Must be able to pass a comprehensive background check, which includes a drug screening.

**DESCRIPTION**:

As a Senior Director of Operations at Thermo Fisher Scientific, you'll manage complex manufacturing operations while driving strategic growth and operational excellence. This key leadership role involves directing production of high-quality products in regulated environments while ensuring exceptional customer service and compliance. You'll optimize end-to-end operations, implement continuous improvement initiatives, and develop high-performing teams aligned with our mission of enabling customers to make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer.

Working closely with cross-functional partners, you'll establish and execute strategic plans, drive productivity and efficiency improvements, and support a culture focused on quality, safety and customer success. This role requires strong business acumen to manage P&L responsibilities while scaling operations to meet growing demand. You'll support our PPI (Practical Process Improvement) business system and 4i values - Integrity, Intensity, Innovation and Involvement - while developing talent and building engaged, collaborative teams.

**REQUIREMENTS**:

* Advanced Degree plus 6 years of experience, or Bachelor's Degree plus 8 years of experience in operations leadership in regulated manufacturing environments
* Preferred Fields of Study: Engineering, Chemistry, Biology, Business or related technical/scientific field
* Advanced training in continuous improvement methodologies (Six Sigma, Lean)
* Demonstrated P&L management and operational excellence experience at scale
* Strong working knowledge of cGMP, FDA, and other relevant quality/regulatory requirements
* Experience leading and developing large, multi-functional teams
* Experience implementing continuous improvement and lean manufacturing methodologies
* Strong business acumen and analytical capabilities
* Effective communication and influence skills across all organizational levels
* Ability to implement change and deliver results in matrix environments
* Experience with ERP systems and manufacturing technologies
* Strong project management capabilities
* Strategic mindset with ability to balance short and long-term priorities
* Experience in customer/client relationship management
* Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities
* Ability to travel 50-75% as required
* Change management and transformation experience
* Cross-functional collaboration and influence skills
* Financial planning and budget management expertise

We offer competitive remuneration, annual incentive plan bonus scheme, healthcare, company 401k, and a range of employee benefits! Thermo Fisher Scientific offers employment with an innovative, forward-thinking organization, and outstanding career and development prospects. We offer an exciting company culture that stands for integrity, intensity, involvement, and innovation.

Thermo Fisher Scientific is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status. Please contact us to request an accommodation.

new_roles.title: Director, Merchandising Operations
new_roles.description:
Parachute Health is transforming post-acute care as the leading digital ordering platform for medical equipment and supplies. We connect major health systems, health plans, and suppliers to help patients get the life-saving products they need at home. Since launching, we've connected 300,000+ clinicians and 3,000+ supplier locations across all 50 states and helped 15M+ patients. What started as a DME ePrescribing tool has become the order management platform of choice for home medical equipment.

Join our team and make a difference in patient care.

### **About the Role**

Parachute Health is building the definitive platform for ordering home medical equipment and supplies, helping clinicians and suppliers ensure that millions of patients each year receive the critical equipment and supplies they need. Our Merchandising Operations team (AKA "Merch") comprises Category Managers and Category Analysts who have three primary jobs: 1) build and maintain our catalog, 2) build and maintain our coverage criteria rules engine, and 3) partner with R&D to improve the tools and workflows behind both. Merch sits at the intersection of e-commerce, compliance, operations, and R&D, and its work is central to Parachute's core functionality. Clinicians use our catalog to find and order the right equipment for their patients, and suppliers rely on it to fulfill those orders. Our coverage criteria help users determine whether an item should be covered by the patient's insurance.

The Merch team's work is nuanced and detail-dense: we maintain information on tens of thousands of products so our software, and the people who use it, can rely on it. The 18-person team splits its time between project work, like building and redesigning product categories and turning payer rules into qualification questions, and ticket-based work, resolving complex requests escalated by our support and partner teams. Our work requires efficient operational processes and excellent documentation.

As Director of Merchandising Operations, you will own the team's operating framework: how work is planned, prioritized, and delivered, and how the team partners with other teams across Parachute. You'll coach and develop a mix of managers and individual contributors, lead the team's largest cross-functional projects, and serve as a close thought partner to the SVP of Merchandising.

The role is primarily internal (roughly 90%), with occasional customer communication, especially on escalations, that calls for a steady, polished hand.

### **What You'll Do**

* Be the operational leader for a highly motivated, highly capable team of managers and individual contributors: keep work running smoothly, protect morale, and learn and add to a team culture that is already strong.
* Drive key projects: stay close to the work and personally drive the team's largest, most complex projects, including timelines, dependencies, and cross-team communication.
* Know every team process end to end. Lead the creation, maintenance, and centralization of SOPs and shared resources; drive consistent practices, training, quality assurance, and continuous improvement across category teams.
* Collaborate with partner teams (e.g., Supplier Implementation, Product, Customer Success) so handoffs and shared processes run smoothly.
* Be a Merch advocate: make the team's work understandable and visible across the company.
* Run bandwidth and capacity planning; flag risks early and rebalance coverage.
* Define and report on team metrics (ticket throughput, SLAs, SKU work, rollout milestones).
* Own escalations as needed, partnering effectively with people at all levels across the organization.
* Support recruiting as needed, own onboarding for new merchants, and maintain continuity coverage for every category.

### **Requirements**

* 7+ years in operations, program delivery, or management or technology consulting (e.g., a Big Four or top-tier firm), with 3+ years managing and growing managers.
* Track record of delivering complex, cross-functional projects using a clear, repeatable methodology.
* Data-driven: comfortable with capacity models, dashboards and prioritization trade-offs.
* Willingness to travel roughly once a quarter.

### **More About You**

* Passionate about improving patient outcomes in the healthcare space.
* Gets things done: drives work to completion and builds processes that stick.
* Thrives in complex, nuanced domains; quickly learns intricate systems (e.g., insurance coverage rules, product data) well enough to make sound calls.
* Clear, concise communicator who pushes back constructively and drives decisions.
* Sound compliance judgment: in a highly regulated industry, you know which issues to resolve and which to escalate.
* Track record of growing into increasing scope and responsibility.
* Nice to have: catalog, product data or e-commerce experience; healthcare, DME/HME or payer experience.

### **Benefits**

* Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage: Comprehensive plans with options for low-to-no-cost premiums
* Employer HSA Contribution: Company-funded contributions to your Health Savings Account
* 401(k) Retirement Plan
* Equity Incentive Plan
* Annual Company-Wide Bonus: Opportunity for up to 15% bonus based on company performance
* Remote-First Culture: We are remote-first with a dedicated NYC office and reimbursement options for co-working spaces
* Flexible Vacation Policy
* Summer Fridays: 5 additional Fridays off during the summer (separate from PTO)
* Home Office and Wellness Stipend
* Monthly Internet Stipend
* Annual Learning and Development Stipend

### **Base Salary Range (based on level and experience)**

$145,000-$180,000

As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

 
 
 

**Local Study Operations Manager (LSOM), Director**
---------------------------------------------------

**What you will do**
--------------------

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role you will provide strategic and operational leadership for the country LSOM organization and is accountable for the quality, timeliness, cost, and compliant execution of the country clinical study portfolio. The role achieves results through LSOM Senior Managers and their FTE and FSP teams, translating global clinical development strategy into country operating priorities. The role directs portfolio delivery, resource and capacity strategy, financial planning, quality and risk management, vendor performance, and inspection readiness from feasibility through study close-out. As a member of the country leadership team, this role influences study placement and portfolio decisions, leads the resolution of significant operational issues, develops organizational capability and succession plans, and represents LSOM operations in country, regional, and global governance forums.

 
 

**Accountabilities**

* Lead the successful delivery of the country study portfolio through the LSOM management organization, ensuring alignment with global clinical development priorities.

* Provides strategic direction and leadership to LSOM country organization across the full study lifecycle, including feasibility, study execution, and study close-out.

* Establishes portfolio-level oversight of delivery, quality, risk, timelines, and performance, directing timely escalation and resolution of critical issues for LSOM management organization.

* Manage LSOM and LSOM vendor performance to guarantee high-quality study execution, serving as the primary escalation point for local study challenges, driving solutions, and ensuring portfolio targets are met within the country.

* Build leadership capability within the LSOM organization through targeted coaching, development, and succession planning, preparing LSOMs to lead increasingly complex trials and programs.

* Establishes strong operating partnerships with Clinical Research Associate (CRA) organization to support study start-up, monitoring, issue resolution, and compliant trial execution across the country portfolio.

* Cultivate a high-performing, accountable, and inclusive organization focused on operational excellence and continuous improvement.

* Champion strong integration between study strategy and local execution teams to translate portfolio priorities into effective country-level delivery.

* Strengthen cross-functional alignment and accountability across country teams to accelerate execution and deliver portfolio commitments.

* Influences study-placement and portfolio investment decisions by providing strategic insight into country's capabilities, operational readiness, performance, and growth potential.

* Anticipates portfolio-level delivery risks, quality trends, and evolving resource requirements, directing mitigation strategies and systemic improvements across country operations.

* Sponsor initiatives that advance operational efficiency, digital innovation, organizational capability, and the adoption of leading practices.

* Direct resource strategy, capacity planning, and workload allocation across FSP and FTE LSOM teams to optimize execution and align resources with global priorities.

* Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory, GCP, ICH, and organizational standards across the country's study portfolio.

Partner with the Regional Head/Country Head and senior cross-functional stakeholders to align priorities, establish accountability for trial deliverables, and resolve significant escalations. 



**Responsibilities**

* Serve as the functional leader for LSOM Senior Managers and the broader LSOM team, including both FSP and FTE, to optimize trial execution and align with global priorities. including strategy and execution, managing risks and escalations

* Partners closely with CRAs, CSPO, Quality, and FSP partners.

* Leads the coordination among country functional teams to ensure successful delivery of the country portfolio.

* Ensure inspection readiness and provide hands-on support during inspections, including responsibility for storyboards.

* Sponsors continuous operational improvement initiatives and encourage sharing of best practices.

* Ensure compliance with relevant regulatory and quality standards.

* Collaborate with the Regional Head/Country Head to engage cross-functional stakeholders, align on trial deliverables, and manage escalations as needed.

**Capability Building and People Leadership**

* Lead, coach, and develop LSOM Sr Managers, including performance management, succession planning, and leadership bench development.

* Build the organizational capabilities, resourcing needed to meet the current and future regional portfolio requirements.

* Foster a high-performing, inclusive, accountable, and patient-focused culture across geographically distributed teams.

* Lead organizational changes and enable adoption of new operating models, technologies

**Authority**

* Accountable for country level oversight and delivery of clinical trials.

* Manage the performance of LSOM Senior Managers and their teams

* Holds line management authority for regional and country operations leaders, including performance management, talent development, succession planning, and capability building.

* Sets regional delivery goals, operating expectations, and performance standards across study start-up, site engagement, monitoring, execution, and closeout.

* Capability build, talent and performance management, and acting as a liaison for cultural differences within region.

**Outputs**

* Manage LSOM resources in accordance with the global study strategy.

* Oversee resource allocation and workload balance across LSOMs.

* Handle FSP supplier resource coordination and monitor performance through quality oversight metrics.

* Identify and report any risks or compliance concerns related to FSP activities.

* Escalate issues to the Regional/Country Head as necessary.

**What we expect of you**

 
 

**Basic Qualifications:**

* Doctorate degree and 4 years of clinical research experience OR
* Master’s degree and 7 years of clinical research experience OR
* Bachelor’s degree and 9 years of clinical research experience

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* 4 years of direct managerial and/or leadership experience or equivalent

* Deep knowledge of ICH GCP, ICH E6(R3), ICH E8(R1), and global regulatory expectations for risk-based monitoring and clinical trial oversight.

* Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and lead complex cross-functional initiatives within a global matrix organization

* Strong Project Management experience

* Experience managing multiple teams / direct reports across multiple clinical functions / trials

* Experience at, or oversight of, clinical research vendors (CROs, central labs, imaging vendors, etc.)

* Experience managing clinical operations across relevant geography / region, including strong understanding of local regulatory requirements around global clinical trials

**What you can expect of us**

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

**Role Overview:**

We are seeking a high-caliber, transformative **Director of Operations** to lead, scale, and optimize our operations. In this role, you will serve as a strategic leader responsible for driving operational excellence, customer advocacy, and regulatory integrity across a multi-faceted organization.

 
 

You will move beyond routine contact center management to steer a dynamic organization comprised of specialized internal operational teams—covering strategic readiness, advanced customer advocacy, and complex fraud/escalation management—alongside large-scale BPO vendor partners managing ~200+ frontline agents.

 
 

You bring a blend of strategic vision, process optimization discipline, vendor governance, and high-impact people leadership required to elevate operational standards and deliver best-in-class customer experiences.

 
 

**You have a proven track record of:**

* **Large-Scale Operations Leadership**: Successfully leading multi-site contact center operations combining internal teams and offshore/nearshore vendor partners of 200+ headcount.
* **Operational Transformation**: Transforming reactive service centers into proactive, quality-focused customer advocacy hubs through structured process engineering.
* **Escalation & Fraud Management**: Effectively mitigating enterprise risk through robust Tier 2 & 3 complaint handling, fraud prevention protocols, and regulatory adherence.
* **Vendor Operations Governance**: Driving rigorous SLA performance, cost efficiency, and quality alignment across third-party BPO vendor organizations.
 

 

**What you’ll do:**

The Director of Operations maintains end-to-end accountability for operational strategy, performance delivery, vendor oversight, and organizational readiness.

* **Leadership Reach**: Direct oversight of Department Managers, Unit Managers (UMs), and Vendor Managers (VMs) across internal and external business units.
* **Core Internal Operations**:
 + **Strategic Operations:** Driving CX quality call listening, 1:1 and group coaching/training, operations readiness, and training materials maintenance.
 + **Customer Advocacy:** Overseeing high-touch inbound customer service, task execution, complex account resolution, and U.S. transfer handling.
 + **Escalations and Fraud**: Leading high-severity escalated problem solving, fraud operations, customer complaint research and resolution, and escalation follow-ups.
* **Core External Operations:**
 + Governance and SLA performance tracking for primary vendor partners overseeing a network of ~200+ non-associate vendor agents performing inbound calls and funding workflows.

 

**Key Focus Areas:**

* Reimagine end to end Operations in this era of AI
* Strategic Leadership & Governance to formulate and execute long-term operational strategies and partner cross functionally
* Partner cross-functionally with Product, Business Analysis, and Process teams to establish and update processes, policies, procedures, and standards
* Define operational KPIs, quality targets, and SLA metrics to ensure consistent service delivery, funding accuracy, and customer satisfaction
* Direct vendor management leads to oversee third-party partners, ensuring ~200+ vendor agents adhere to operational guidelines and productivity benchmarks
* Risk, Fraud, & Complaint Resolution spanning complex problem solving and root-cause analysis
* Ensure business readiness for product launches, process updates, and technology enhancements across all operational sub-functions
* Mentor, develop, and inspire a multi-layered leadership team, cultivating a culture of accountability, continuous learning, and high performance.
* Optimize talent allocation and capacity planning across teams to handle volume fluctuations dynamically.
 

 

**Location:** Plano, TX - This role is designated as a hybrid position. You are expected to adhere to Capital One's hybrid policy regarding required on-site presence at your designated office location.

new_roles.title: Field Operations Director
new_roles.description:
### **The Position**

From the beginning, Genentech has been a team of highly dedicated, passionate individuals. We are a place where people are united around a single purpose and an ambitious vision. Together, we aspire to deliver ever better health outcomes for patients while lowering overall healthcare costs. Our goal is to compel the customer to act on behalf of their patients while showing great commitment to the rare disease community, whose support is key. Utilizing innovative methods to identify patients who may benefit from treatment, we must take a highly strategic approach to patient access while assisting patients and their caregivers to navigate the healthcare system.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Field Operations Director serves as the trusted operations partner to an assigned Regional VP or National Team VP and their leadership team, helping translate business priorities into clear plans, coordinated execution, and effective connection to the broader CE Operations and enterprise support network. The Director owns the operating rhythm and priority agenda for the assigned leadership team and provides a single point of connectivity between Field Leadership and the broader operational ecosystem.

SCOPE & KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategic Partnership with Field Leadership

* Serve as the primary Operations partner to an assigned Regional VP or National Team VP and their leadership team.
* Develop a deep understanding of the team's business priorities, customers, opportunities, challenges, and performance.
* Translate enterprise and CE priorities into clear implications and action plans for the assigned Region or National Team.
* Provide strategic and operational counsel to leadership and proactively identify issues requiring attention, decisions, or escalation.
* Help leadership prioritize competing needs and maintain focus on the highest-impact business opportunities.

Operating Rhythm & Business Planning

* Own the operating rhythm and priority agenda for the assigned leadership team.
* Lead development and coordination of annual, quarterly, and other operating plans.
* Translate priorities into clear roadmaps with owners, milestones, dependencies, and measures of progress.
* Coordinate leadership agendas, decision materials, action tracking, and follow-through.
* Support Regional or National Team input into ABP, resource planning, RBO, and other CE and enterprise planning processes.

Operational Integration & Execution

* Serve as a front door for operational requests from the assigned leadership team and route needs to the appropriate CE Operations or enterprise partner.
* Connect Field Leadership and HEDs to the broader support network without requiring them to independently navigate multiple teams.
* Coordinate across Enterprise Operations, RBO, Squad Field Partners, ABP, DDA, L&SD, and other functions to enable execution.
* Anticipate execution barriers, dependencies, and operational risks and mobilize partners to resolve them.
* Ensure appropriate communication and coordination between enterprise initiatives and Regional/National execution.

Insights & Decision Support

* Synthesize field insights, performance signals, customer information, and emerging business needs into clear leadership implications.
* Develop business reviews and decision materials that enable productive leadership conversations.
* Identify patterns and recurring needs that may have implications beyond the assigned Region or National Team.
* Surface cross-field opportunities, risks, and common needs to the Head of CE Field Operations so they can be addressed across the organization where appropriate.
* Provide recommendations related to priorities, resources, capacity, and operational tradeoffs.

Resource & Capacity Planning

* Maintain an integrated understanding of the assigned team's resource and capacity requirements.
* Support Regional or National Team roster, resource, and capacity planning.
* Identify capacity constraints and emerging needs and develop recommendations in partnership with Field Leadership.
* Connect local resource needs to broader CE and enterprise planning processes.

KEY DELIVERABLES

* Annual and quarterly operating plans
* Regional or National Team priority roadmap
* Leadership agendas, decision materials, and action logs
* Business reviews and synthesized field insights
* RBO, ABP, and enterprise planning inputs
* Resource, roster, and capacity plans
* Consolidated requests, risks, and capacity recommendations
* Clear escalation of cross-field opportunities and common operational needs

MINDSET & CAPABILITIES

* Trusted partner who builds credibility with senior Field Leaders
* Strategic thinker with strong operational discipline
* Able to translate ambiguity and complexity into clear plans and actions
* Strong business acumen and understanding of field execution
* Highly effective at influencing without formal authority
* Skilled at connecting people, priorities, and resources across organizational boundaries
* Strong analytical and synthesis capabilities
* Proactive and anticipatory rather than reactive
* Comfortable navigating a complex, matrixed environment
* Strong judgment and ability to distinguish between issues that should be solved locally and those requiring enterprise solutions
* Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining focus on business impact
* Growth mindset and commitment to continuous improvement

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

* Bachelor's degree required
* Significant pharmaceutical, biotechnology, consulting, commercial, field operations, strategic, and/or analytical experience (8+ years preferred)
* Demonstrated experience partnering with senior business or field leaders
* Experience translating strategy into operational plans and driving execution
* Strong project/program management and cross-functional leadership capabilities
* Demonstrated ability to operate effectively within a complex matrixed organization
* Strong communication, executive presentation, analytical, and problem-solving skills
* Ability and willingness to travel as required for internal and external business meetings

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

new_roles.title: Regional Operations Director
new_roles.description:
### **Your Impact as a Regional Operations Director**

As a Regional Operations Director, you are a key leader responsible for the success and health of a diverse portfolio of veterinary hospitals. You will serve as the crucial link between local hospital teams and the broader Mission Pet Health network, empowering your teams to achieve excellence in both business performance and patient care.

* **Champion a Thriving Culture:** You'll partner with your Regional Medical Director to foster a positive, engaged, and high-performing culture across all hospitals in your region.
* **Develop Future Leaders:** You'll guide the growth of Hospital Managers and their teams, ensuring a strong pipeline of talent through effective coaching, training, and career development.
* **Drive Business Performance:** You'll have full ownership of the financial health of your region, managing P&Ls to drive revenue growth and optimize operational efficiency.
* **Build Winning Teams:** You'll lead the strategy for non-DVM recruiting and staffing, ensuring your hospitals have the talent they need to succeed.
* **Elevate the Client Experience:** You'll set the standard for exceptional client service, ensuring operational processes support a seamless and positive experience for every pet owner.

### **What You'll Bring to the Team**

* A proven track record of successful multi-site P&L management, with a keen ability to drive financial results.
* Demonstrated success in recruiting, developing, and retaining high-performing teams, especially in a leadership capacity.
* Exceptional leadership skills with a talent for building a positive, accountable, and solutions-focused culture.
* Excellent communication and conflict management skills, with the ability to tailor messages to diverse audiences.
* Significant experience leading in a multi-site veterinary, healthcare, or customer-centric retail environment.

### **How You're Supported**

*As part of the Mission Pet Health family, you get the stability of a local practice backed by the comprehensive benefits and resources of a larger network. The focus is on investing in you, so you can focus on what you love.* 
 
*Note: Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to support you at every stage. Eligibility for specific benefits varies based on your role and hours worked.*

##### **Competitive Compensation**

A competitive hourly rate or salary based on your experience and role.

##### **Health & Wellbeing**

We offer comprehensive coverage options including Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance, along with access to our Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for all teammates.

##### **Financial Security**

Plan for your future with our 401k retirement options and additional financial protection benefits like Life Insurance and Disability coverage.

##### **Commitment to Growth**

We support your career goals with opportunities for professional development, including educational assistance for qualified teammates to enroll in AVMA-accredited veterinary technician programs.

##### **The Power of a Network**

Join a nationwide community of over 20,000 veterinary professionals who share a passion for collaboration, career growth, and sharing best practices.

##### **Valuable Perks**

Enjoy discounted veterinary care for your own pets, access to an online discount platform, and free 24/7 access to doctors through Teladoc.

### **About Mission Pet Health**

Mission Pet Health was founded by veterinarians on the belief that local practices thrive with clinical autonomy, collaboration, and medical excellence. The organization provides world-class support to its 850+ hospital teams on a hyper-local basis so they can focus on what matters most: the medicine, their patients, and their team culture. Learn more at **missionpethealth.com**.

Driving the award-winning culture are the WAG values – **Work Together, Amaze, and Grow**. Mission Pet Health is veterinarian-led, people-focused, and on a mission to be the best place to work in veterinary medicine. We are proud to be recognized as a 2025 "Most Loved Workplace," ranked #2 in America's Top 100 and #1 in veterinary care.

**Reasonable Accommodations:** Applicants with disabilities may be entitled to reasonable accommodation. Please contact benefits@mvetpartners.com with your request and contact information.

**EEO Statement:** Mission Pet Health is an equal opportunity employer. We embrace diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.
